recipes.name: Frogmore Stew
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds hot smoked sausage links, cut into 2 inch pieces
12 ears corn - husked, cleaned and quartered

steps.text: Bring water and Old Bay seasoning to a boil in a large stockpot over high heat.
Add potatoes; cook for 15 minutes. Add sausage; cook for 5 more minutes. Add corn; cook for 5 more minutes. Stir in shrimp; cook until shrimp are pink, about 5 minutes. Drain immediately and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Frogmore Stew
raw_recipe.description: Frogmore stew is a traditional South Carolina low country boil made with unpeeled shrimp, corn on the cob, new red potatoes, and hot smoked sausage.

review.reviewBody:
I made this exact dish 01/01/06....but with King Crab Legs! It is a good dish, but a fun dish. and I think that those who did not like it, did not (1) know how to serve it, (2) it is NOT a stew! The name is misleading because there is no gravy to speak of, it is just boiled food in one pot, but very tasty.

It is just an "ole Fashion" crab .... shrimp, boil! with your entire meal in one pot! I think this recipe had a few mistakes in it. You should start with the corn on the cob (regardless if it is fresh or frozen) First, because it takes longer to cook, actually I boiled my corn in a separate pot, and in my main pot I had the bay seasoning boiling. Then I'd commence to add the potatoes, and then the sausage, and in the last 4 minutes I threw in the seafood, and my already cooked corn.

You're close! Add a bag of Zatarains crab boil and a full cup of Old Bay. It's not hot but gives off much more flavor. Secondly, I use 2 different kinds of sausage for folks who like it hot and folks that don't. Cut the Roger Woods Hot into 1' pieces and the Roger Woods mild into 2" pieces to differentiate. lastly 5 minutes is too long for the Shrimp. Cut off the gas and stir in for 3 minutes. Drain and dump immediately since they continue cooking in the shell. By the way, get a Bayou Classic pot with a strainer basket! So much easier.

This was RIDICULOUSLY good and easy. I overlooked the "large stock pot" notation both times I read the recipe through; luckily, seeing the six quarts of water ingredient, I halved the recipe.

The only subs I made were to cut things into one-inch lengths and subbed one pound of raw medium hot Italian sausage in addition to a pound of kielbasa because I had it on hand; I added a bit of cayenne to make up the anticipated difference in heat. I figured since the mixture would be boiling away for a while, I would throw it in with the potatoes step and since the whole thing is drained at the end, it gets rid of the grease. Win-win.

When it was time to add the shrimp, there was no room left in the pot, so I transferred some of the liquid into a sauce pan and did the shrimp separately. I then used a slotted spoon to move the shrimp into the large pot again (since there was room due to the reduction of the amount of fluid in the pot).

The only criticism, if you can call it that, is that I felt the shrimp added nothing to the recipe. Since that may have been because of the method I had to use, no deduction there.

My new, MUCH larger stock pot arrives today. I will be making this again and again and again. The next time, I am going to double the potatoes and eliminate the shrimp. In fact, there's a lot of room to experiment with different textures and flavors.

The most incredible surprise was the corn-on-the-cob. Unbelievable flavor; so much so, that I will add Old Bay to the water

I ripped this recipe from my AllRecipes magazine to make this summer for our shared, multi-family meal while on vacation. It was a hit! Everyone loved it! We did this outside using our turkey-fryer (used water). By chopping everything ahead of time (potatoes, sausage, corn) and using a timer (easy to get distracted when hosting) - could drop all ingredients in as indicated in the recipe. Other than adding a few ounces of Zatarans Seafood Boil oil to the water and some quartered onions, followed exactly. Huge hit. Repeated again for another family get-together with equally raving results! We didn’t either time but will consider adding some chopped cabbage. A not-so-healthy add; take a dozen hard-boiled eggs chopped and sauté in some butter. Serve over corn or potatoes. Delicious!! Thank you Shirley for this awesome recipe. Will make for many special events moving forward!

holy moly!!!! this is sooooo yummy. we made this last night for the 4th of july and have now claimed it as our new 4th of july tradition! i am already planning to have it next weekend again when my in laws come to town! i preped everything ahead of time so when it can time to start cooking it was a breeze! i started of my boil with 8 qts of water, 2 beers, 2 lemeons halved, 1 cup of old bay and 2 T. of garlic! i used fingerling potatoes , 1 lb shrimp its a must to have the shells on, 2 lb of crab legs, 4 ears of corn halved and cajun sauage! i would give these 500 stars if i could. thnaks for sharing.

Everyone loved it. I had to divide these proportion into 3 batches since I only had a 12 quart pot. It was perfect though because as people showed up, there was always a fresh hot batch ready to be eaten. Like others did, I added lemon, onions, garlic and beer (2 cans per 6oz water) to the water. I also added mussels in 5 minutes after the corn, then added the shrimp. It was mmmmm mmmmm delish.

Instead of the Old Bay, I used a package of the Zatarain's seafood boil mix in a bag. Otherwise I followed other suggestions of throwing in a quartered onion, a lemon, some garlic cloves, baby carrots and substituting beer for some of the water. I adjusted the recipe for 6 servings which gave us a lot of corn and we would have preferred more sausage. Flavor was good - quite a bit spicy! Everything cooked up beautifully - cooked the potatoes for about 10 minutes, added corn and carrots for 5 minutes, then sausage for 5 and finally shrimp and removed from heat. Very good but I will try with just the Old Bay next time.

Agree with another reviewer that five minutes is too long to cook the shrimp. Once I add the shrimp, I watch it closely, and certainly remove it as soon as the water comes back to a boil, if not before then. Remember that the shrimp will keep cooking somewhat even after you’ve taken it out of the pot. If you want to take this over the top, pour on a little highly concentrated shrimp stock at the end. ( I save up shrimp heads and shells to make stock.)

I use sweet Italian sausage and started with a beer old bay and some water. I cooked the Ingredients for 10 minutes each before adding the next. This has always been a big hit with family and friends.

Yummm! I cut this recipe in half to feed six and have enough leftovers for two. Essentially followed the recipe with some tweaks others have recommended - added a can of beer, some garlic and lemon juice to the water. Cut all ingredients in half. Gave corn and potatoes a little extra cooking time -- added them first for 10 minutes before adding sausage for 10 minutes. Added shrimp last and only cooked about three minutes til they changed color -- I agree not to overcook the shrimp!!! Drained, squeezed some lemon and sprinkled some parsley on top and served with warm buttered French bread (and beer). Delicious!!! I was concerned it might be too spicy, but it's not.

This rocks! I've made similar recipes before that lacked flavor. I made some changes. I Halfed this recipie but still used 1/2 c Old Bay. I used regular smoked sausage, so for extra flavor I replaced 1/3 of water with beer (one 32 ounce can) added a lemon, lime, onion, celery and two large cloves of smashed garlic. I changed the order and added my corn before my sausage so it would not dry out. Next time I'll add a bit more sausage and shrimp! All I had left were the corn and potatoes.
Great as I can make one small portion for me or for many. Always delicious.
Ummm this is called a low country boil in the South

Add the shrimp and immediately turn off the heat and cover the pot. Wait about 5 minutes, and they will be perfect. Cut the sausage after boiling, rather than before, to prevent the juices from boiling out.
I moved to Beaufort SC in 1989. The friends we were staying with made this for dinner the first night. Our friend had been out shrimping for the shrimp was fresh and our dinner was delicious!

I use three cans of lite beer and three cans of water to boil everything. Gives it a much better flavor. I also add crab legs. You can add scallops, muscles, craw fish, oysters... whatever seafood you like. Here in SC we add a hard boiled egg or two, as well.
